submitted.rationale: Index 0 (Fe0.84Sb0.16) had the highest measured EQE, 0.108%. Along the line, EQE drops steadily as Sb rises: 0.053% at index 3 and 0.005% at index 13. This fits Sb-doped hematite being the active absorber at 2.7 eV, with photoactivity lost as the material becomes FeSbO4 and FeSb2O6 at higher Sb.

rejected.reason: Measured 0.005% EQE. FeSbO4 is stable (MACE) and has a 2.08 eV gap (MEGNet) but performs poorly.
Measured 0.053% EQE, lower than index 0, which confirms the monotonic trend.
Not measured. MEGNet predicts a narrow 1.28 eV gap, and EQE was already falling with more Sb.

consultations.verdict: Support. Fe-rich end should be Sb-doped hematite; MEGNet gap for Fe2O3 (2.77 HSE, known overestimate of ~2.1 eV) and FeSbO4 (2.08) both indicate absorption at 2.7 eV. FeSbO4 is on hull (MACE 0.002 eV/atom), so mid-line will be FeSbO4 rutile. Fe-rich hematite with Sb donor doping is the classic best photoanode here; measure index 0 first as anchor.

Mixed support. MACE puts FeSb2O6 on the hull (0.0 eV/atom). FeSbO4 is also near the hull, from the earlier receipt. MEGNet predicts FeSb2O6 has a narrow 1.28 eV gap, probably too small and prone to recombination. FeSbO4 (2.08 eV) looks like the better absorber at 2.7 eV. Index 13 (Fe 0.516) is close to the FeSbO4 stoichiometry, so I'll use it to test the mid-line phase.

Weak support. Hematite is an absorber at 2.7 eV (MEGNet PBE gap 1.53, which underestimates; the real gap is about 2.1). The measurements show EQE falling steeply from Fe-rich (0.108%) to FeSbO4 (0.005%), so the best region is the hematite-rich end. Index 3 (Fe 0.79) tests whether a local optimum exists below index 0's Sb level. MEGNet can't tell apart these doping levels, so on that question the model is uninformative.
